title: Big trades & bubbles: tape, thresholds, clustering and the bubble overlay
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#6-r2--order-flow-beta`, sprints S10–S13, `v0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E22 Big trades & bubbles** is the *aggression* layer of that release. Roadmap scope line (§6.2): "Threshold configuration (absolute, notional, or percentile-of-session); bubble overlay sized by volume and coloured by aggressor side; big-trade list panel with click-to-locate; per-symbol threshold memory; sweep/block grouping within a configurable time window" — **21 pts, Sprint S12**, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`orderflow`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` — `server/orderflow/` hosts footprint, profile, cvd, imbalance, heatmap, **tape**), story domain **BIG**.

The decisive simplification, stated in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §"The tape": **Bybit publishes the aggressor side directly (`S`)**, so no tick-rule reconstruction is needed and a print's side is exact, not estimated. Consequently the tape, the bubbles and the big-trade alerts are all **exact** views — the only `(estimated)` surface in this epic is `trade_cluster` (§ metric table: `trade_cluster` — "Prints within `window_ms` at same price/side treated as one aggressor", `window_ms=50`, confidence **estimated**), which is why CMP-227 EstimatedBadge appears on SCR-053 whenever clustering is on.

The second invariant is single-source evaluation: US-BIG-002's NFR says "*thresholds per symbol; evaluation backend-side so tape, bubbles and alerts agree*", and US-BIG-004's NFR says "*deterministic and unit-tested; clustering happens once, backend-side*". There is therefore exactly one `BigTradeEngine` in M9 and three renderers of its output (tape rows, chart bubbles, alert conditions). A second client-side threshold implementation is an explicit anti-goal of this epic.

Dependency per the roadmap graph (§11.1): `E08 --> E22` — E08 Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton owns `publicTrade` normalisation (US-MKT-006) and the in-process bus. E11/E12 supply the chart-engine series-plugin surface the bubble layer plugs into (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Bubbles | instanced circles (SDF disc) | `disc` | 1 | Radius by notional, alpha by age"). E16 Recorder supplies the tape history behind `GET /market/trades` and percentile windows; global AC #7 (partial-history state) applies wherever we read recorded history.


**Sizing reconciliation.** The roadmap sizes E22 at **21 pts** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` lines 122 and 313). Engineering points here are the sum of the Story/Task/Spike children: S01 3 + S02 1 + S03 2 + S04 1 + S05 1 + S06 2 = 10 (Story), T01 5 + T02 2 + T03 1 + T04 2 = 10 (Task), K01 2 (Spike) = **22 pts**, i.e. +4.8% against the roadmap figure and inside the allowed ±15% band (17.85–24.15). The Epic `estimate` field (52) is the rollup of **all** children including the design (D), QA (Q) and security (X) tickets, which are staffed from the design/QA/security capacity lines and are not part of the roadmap's engineering figure.

**Design-ahead compliance.** The design chain runs D01 (S07) → D02/D03 (S08) → D04/D05 (S09); the E22-D05 handoff pack is Status=Done by the end of Sprint 09, two full sprints before the consuming frontend stories E22-S01..S05 start in Sprint 12. The ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1/§3.1) is therefore satisfied by schedule and **no Architect/CDO waiver is recorded or required**. E22-D06 (design QA of the built result, S13) is deliberately downstream and is not a design-ahead input.
## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories covered:** US-BIG-001 (Must, time & sales tape), US-BIG-002 (Must, big-trade threshold highlighting), US-BIG-003 (Must, bubble plotting on the chart), US-BIG-004 (Must, print clustering), US-BIG-006 (Should, tape filters and columns), US-BIG-005 (Should, big-trade alerts — deferred to Backlog because its `Deps` include US-ALRT-004, which lands with E40 in R3).
- **Screens:** SCR-053 Tape / Time & Sales + big-trade bubbles panel (the epic's home screen); SCR-091 Alert editor (big-trade condition, deferred story only); SCR-030 Chart panel hosts the bubble overlay.
- **Components:** CMP-112 BigTradeBubble (chart primitive, built on CMP-195 AnnotationMarker), CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend (M9):** `BigTradeEngine` — threshold evaluation (absolute size / USDT notional / rolling percentile) and deterministic print clustering; metric descriptors `big_trade_notional`, `big_trade_zscore`, `trade_cluster` registered in the `MetricRegistry` (`24-internal-schemas.md` order-flow metric table).
- **Contracts:** WS topic `trades.{symbol}` with options `min_size`, `cluster_window_ms`, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1), payload `TradesBatch` (§14.2 — `cluster_size`, `is_block_trade`, `dropped`), binary `body_kind 3` (22-byte records, `flags` bit2 = cluster-aggregated); REST `GET /market/trades` (`min_size`, `cluster_window_ms`, `cluster_tolerance_ticks`, `side`) and `GET /market/metrics` (`metric=big_trade_notional|big_trade_zscore`).
- **Data:** QuestDB `trades` (with precomputed `notional` — "Typical queries: … `WHERE notional > x` for big-trade bubbles", `21-database-schema.md` §4.1); Postgres `settings` (scope `user`, keys `bigtrade.*`) for per-symbol threshold memory; `chart_templates`/`layout_panes` for tape column sets.
- **Design:** full design track for SCR-053 and CMP-112, scheduled S10–S11 (≥2 sprints ahead of the S12 engineering work), plus a design-QA sweep in S13.
- **QA:** black-box plan, exploratory charter, Playwright E2E additions, a 2 000 prints/s perf script, a11y audit, epic regression pack and sign-off.
- **Security:** STRIDE model for the epic and a review of the tape/export/threshold surfaces.

## Out of scope
- **US-BIG-005 big-trade alerts** — story exists here (E22-S06) but is parked in `Backlog` until E40 Alerts (R3) lands `US-ALRT-004` alert centre. E22 ships the *metric* (`big_trade_notional`) that E40 will consume.
- Iceberg / stop-run / absorption detection — E25 Detectors.
- Speed of tape and the tape-speed gauge (SCR-055, CMP-131/CMP-187) — E25.
- Liquidation prints and liquidation markers (CMP-127, `liquidations.{symbol}`) — E24.
- CVD and per-bar delta — E23. Footprint cells — E18.
- Any trading action from a tape row (click-to-trade) — E31.
- Android, a separate admin app, non-Bybit venues, non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One threshold, three surfaces
  Given the BTCUSDT big-trade threshold is 250 000 USDT notional
  When a 300 000 USDT print arrives on the trades.BTCUSDT topic
  Then the tape row is highlighted, a bubble is drawn at that price and time, and the big_trade_notional metric reports the same print
  And all three read the same backend-evaluated flag, with no client-side threshold re-implementation

Scenario: Clustering is deterministic and honest
  Given cluster_window_ms = 250 and cluster_tolerance_ticks = 1
  When the same recorded window is replayed twice
  Then the emitted clusters are byte-identical across runs
  And every clustered view renders the (estimated) badge (CMP-227) with a popover naming window, tolerance and constituent count

Scenario: Density does not break the frame budget
  Given 5 000 qualifying bubbles are visible and the tape is receiving 2 000 prints/s
  Then the chart holds >= 55 fps, the tape holds >= 55 fps with <= 60 rows in the DOM
  And the visible coalescing factor and the dropped-print count are shown rather than silently swallowed

Scenario: Epic exit
  Given every child ticket is Done
  Then coverage floors hold (>= 85% M9/engine, >= 80% web), zero open P0/P1 against E22 scope
  And axe-core is green on SCR-053 with a manual screen-reader pass recorded, design sign-off is Done, STRIDE findings are triaged, and the Owner accepts at Sprint Review
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Engine placement:** `server/orderflow/bigtrade.py` subscribes to the normalised trade stream from E08 (US-MKT-006 — `{ts, price, qty, side, tradeId}`, idempotent by `tradeId`). It is a pure function of the trade stream plus a per-symbol config, which is what makes replay determinism achievable.
- **Threshold modes:** `absolute_size` (base units), `notional` (price*size USDT, matching `trades.notional` in QuestDB), `percentile` (rank over a rolling window, default 1 h, refreshed at most every 5 s). The *effective absolute* threshold is always published alongside the mode so the UI can show it (US-BIG-002 scenario 2).
- **Clustering:** a per-(symbol, side, price-bucket) open cluster with a `window_ms` deadline and `tolerance_ticks` bucket width; a print joins the open cluster if same side and within tolerance of the cluster's anchor price and inside the deadline, otherwise the cluster is emitted and a new one opens. Bar attribution rule (US-BIG-004 scenario 3): the cluster belongs to the bar containing its **first** print.
- **Wire:** `TradesBatch.cluster_size` and `flags` bit2 carry clustering; `dropped` carries prints filtered by `min_size` ("never silent", §14.2).
- **Rendering:** bubbles are a chart-engine series plugin using the `disc` program with instanced draws; LOD per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Bubbles | Size-threshold raising as density grows; cluster into a single bubble with a count badge | Keep <= 500 visible instances".
- **Persistence:** thresholds in `settings` (`scope='user'`, keys `bigtrade.threshold_mode`, `bigtrade.threshold_value`, `bigtrade.cluster_window_ms`, `bigtrade.cluster_tolerance_ticks`, per-symbol object values); key format must satisfy `st_key_fmt` (`^[a-z0-9_]+([.][a-z0-9_]+){0,4}$`).

## Test plan
Unit (threshold modes, percentile estimator, clustering state machine, bar attribution), contract (OpenAPI + WS JSON-schema for `TradesBatch` and binary kind 3), integration against recorded Bybit fixtures (normal session, volatility burst, WS disconnect+resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol), golden-fixture parity vs an offline DuckDB recomputation over the Parquet tier (R2 exit criterion #6 pattern), E2E (Playwright: filter, pause, click-to-locate, threshold change), perf (2 000 prints/s tape, 5 000-bubble scene), determinism (double-replay cluster equality), a11y (axe + manual SR).

## Security notes
Threats per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: (S) none new — market data is public and unauthenticated market topics still require a session; (T) tampering with thresholds via unvalidated `settings` writes; (R) repudiation — threshold changes are user settings and emit `settings.change` audit entries; (I) information disclosure is low (public market data, classification **public**); (D) **denial of service is the real risk** — an unbounded `GET /market/trades` window, `cluster_window_ms` extremes or a `min_size=0` subscription on a hot symbol can pin CPU or flood the socket; (E) none. Controls: parameter bounds already in the OpenAPI (`cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, `Limit`), cursor pagination, per-connection subscription caps, `dropped` counters, RBAC `marketdata:read` on both endpoints. Epic carries the `security` label; X01/X02 deliver the STRIDE model and the review.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-053: tape is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default, opt-in polite announcements **for whale prints only**; rows individually focusable and readable. CMP-112 uses the sparse DOM-mirror marker contract with `aria-label` of the form "Big sell, 42,000 USDT, 65,410, 14:32:01". Size tiers must be conveyed by weight/glyph as well as colour (global AC #3, no colour-only meaning); the `(estimated)` badge's accessible name contains the literal word "estimated". Filter chips are keyboard-removable (CMP-011/CMP-055); column reorder supports `Alt+↑/↓` (CMP-056).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #1 frame time ≤16.6 ms p95 with the full order-flow scene, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 **WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate)**, #5 ingestion with zero loss. Story NFRs: tape ≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s with a 10 000-print ring buffer and ≤60 DOM rows; bubbles ≥55 fps with 5 000 visible (instanced); alert emission ≤500 ms from print. §6 degradation playbook item 3 explicitly allows coalescing big-trade-bubble redraws to every 2nd frame.

## Observability
Metrics: `bigtrade_prints_evaluated_total{symbol}`, `bigtrade_flagged_total{symbol,mode}`, `bigtrade_clusters_emitted_total{symbol}`, `bigtrade_eval_latency_seconds` histogram, `tape_frames_coalesced_total`, `tape_prints_dropped_total{reason="min_size"}`. Analytics events from SCR-053: `tape.filter_changed`, `tape.paused`, `tape.resumed`, `tape.print_clicked`. Audit: `settings.change` for threshold edits. Traces: span `orderflow.bigtrade.evaluate` inside the ingest→bus span.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 (Epic DoD): all children Done or explicitly descoped; epic-level AC verified end-to-end; coverage floors green; docs (`14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`) reflect shipped behaviour; WCAG 2.2 AA verified on SCR-053 (axe CI + manual SR pass); perf numbers recorded against budgets #1/#3; STRIDE finalised and findings triaged with Security sign-off; epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass recorded; demoed to Owner at Sprint Review against staging (demo); retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
- `E08` Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton — normalised `publicTrade` stream, sequence-gap handling, in-process bus (roadmap edge `E08 --> E22`).
- `E11`/`E12` chart engine core & series rendering — the series-plugin surface, picking index and price/time scales the bubble layer plugs into.
- `E16` Recorder — tape history for `GET /market/trades`, percentile windows and the partial-history state (global AC #7).
- `E15` Layouts — persistence of the tape pane, its column set and filters.
- `E17` WS protocol — `trades.{symbol}` topic plumbing, binary framing, throttling/coalescing semantics.
- `E40` Alerts (R3) — consumer of `big_trade_notional`; blocks the parked E22-S06 only.

## Branch
`feat/e22-big-trades-<short>` (e.g. `feat/e22-big-trades-engine`). PRs ≤400 LOC diff; split backend engine, contract change, tape panel and bubble layer into separate PRs.

## References

title: UX research: how traders read the tape and size on the chart
body:
## Context
E22 introduces SCR-053 (Tape / Time & Sales + big-trade bubbles panel) — a net-new interaction surface: a high-rate scrolling print feed plus a chart overlay of size markers. Before wireframes are drawn we need evidence on how the Owner and the account managers (`docs/plan/10-personas.md` P1 order-flow trader, M1 manager) actually read aggression: which columns they scan first, at what density they stop being able to read rows, whether they prefer pause-on-hover or an explicit pause, and what threshold they instinctively reach for. Design runs ≥2 sprints ahead of the S12 engineering work (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` design-ahead rule), so this lands in Sprint 10.

Relevant story NFRs that the research must pressure-test: US-BIG-001 ("2 000 prints per second … the tape coalesces per frame … and shows the coalescing factor"), US-BIG-002 scenario 3 ("threshold would flag more than 20% of prints → a warning suggests raising it"), US-BIG-003 ("radius scaled by notional (linear or log)"), US-BIG-006 (filters and column set).

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3–4 moderated sessions (Owner + ≥2 account managers) using a clickable/recorded prototype of a live tape at 3 print rates (50/s, 500/s, 2 000/s) and a chart with bubbles at 3 densities.
- Findings memo in `docs/plan/` research notes referenced from SCR-053, covering: preferred column order and default column set; readable row density (compact vs comfortable); pause model (hover vs explicit `P`); size-tier encoding preference (weight/glyph/colour combinations); linear vs log bubble scaling defaults; default threshold mode (absolute / notional / percentile) and starting values per symbol class.
- A recommended default configuration for SCR-053 that D02 will wireframe.
- Explicit list of open questions handed to D02 as design hypotheses.

## Out of scope
- Visual design, tokens, hi-fi comps (D02/D03).
- Speed-of-tape gauge (E25), liquidation prints (E24), click-to-trade from a tape row (E31).
- Quantitative analytics instrumentation (the `tape.*` analytics events ship with E22-S01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed
  Given a prototype showing tape rates of 50, 500 and 2000 prints per second
  When at least three participants including the Owner have completed a session
  Then a findings memo records, per participant, the readable density ceiling and the preferred column order

Scenario: A default configuration is recommended
  When the research is synthesised
  Then a single recommended default column set, density, pause model, bubble scale and threshold mode is stated with the evidence for each choice

Scenario: A hypothesis is contradicted
  Given the pre-registered hypothesis that traders prefer log bubble scaling
  When participants disagree
  Then the memo records the disagreement, the chosen default, and a follow-up question for D06 design QA rather than silently keeping the hypothesis
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype can be a throwaway React harness replaying a recorded BTCUSDT fixture (the same recorded-session fixtures listed in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) — it does not need the real engine. Record sessions with consent; store notes with participant initials only.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity controls: pre-registered hypotheses, same fixture window per participant, questions asked in fixed order.

## Security notes
Session recordings may contain account context on screen — use a demo account and redact any account identifiers before storing. Data classification: internal.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session run keyboard-only and one with the OS screen reader active, to ground the `role="log"` / `aria-live="off"` decision documented in SCR-053 before it is locked in D02.

## Performance notes
The prototype must reproduce the real print rates (up to 2 000/s) or the density findings are worthless; instrument it to report the actual achieved rate.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
Findings memo merged and linked from the SCR-053 entry; recommended defaults accepted by the Chief Design Officer; open questions filed onto E22-D02; sessions and consent recorded; no engineering ticket in E22 quotes a default that contradicts the memo without a recorded waiver.

## Dependencies
`E08` supplies the recorded trade fixtures used by the prototype.

## Branch

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for tape and bubbles
body:
## Context
A scrolling tape and appearing/fading bubbles are the two most motion-heavy surfaces in R2 outside the heatmap, and both are exactly the kind of continuous motion that harms users with vestibular sensitivity. Global AC #3 requires `prefers-reduced-motion` to be honoured, and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (WCAG 2.2 AA) plus the SCR-053 a11y contract (`role="log"`, `aria-live="off"` by default, opt-in polite announcements for whale prints only) must be turned into an implementable spec before E22-S01/S03 start.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec: tape row insertion (no per-row animation at high rate — specify the rate above which insertion animation is disabled entirely), new-bubble appear transition, alpha-by-age decay curve and duration, whale-print emphasis pulse, pause/resume transition, and the reduced-motion variant of each (static insert, no pulse, no decay animation — value snaps).
- Announcement policy: exactly which events are announced, at what throttle, and the announcement text template for a whale print; the off-by-default state and where the opt-in lives (SCR-053 header / settings a11y section).
- Keyboard spec: `P` pause/resume, `Ctrl+F` filter focus, `↑/↓` row navigation with focus retained while paused, `Enter` = click-to-locate (jump the synced crosshair), `Esc` clears the filter, `Alt+↑/↓` column reorder.
- Focus-management spec for the transition into and out of the paused state (focus must not be lost when rows are frozen or released).
- a11y review sign-off against `05-accessibility-standard.md` for SCR-053 and CMP-112.

## Out of scope
Implementation; the axe/manual audit of the built screen (E22-Q04); design QA of the built screen (E22-D06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is fully specified
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the spec is applied
  Then every animation in the tape and bubble layer has a defined static or instantaneous alternative, and none is left to implementer discretion

Scenario: Announcements cannot flood
  Given 2000 prints per second with announcements opted in
  Then at most one announcement per configured throttle interval is emitted and only whale prints qualify

Scenario: Focus survives pause
  Given a tape row has keyboard focus
  When the tape is paused and then resumed
  Then focus remains on the same print, and the buffered-print count is announced once
```

## Technical notes / design
Do not animate row insertion by translating the list — at 2 000 prints/s the list is virtualised and coalesced per frame, so any per-row transform is both invisible and expensive. Specify emphasis as an opacity/weight state on the already-painted row instead.

## Test plan
Spec is validated by the Playwright + axe checks written in E22-Q02/E22-Q04 — each spec line must map to an assertion.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable: WCAG 2.2 AA criteria explicitly addressed — 1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.1 use of colour, 2.1.1 keyboard, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.8 target size ≥24×24, 4.1.3 status messages.

## Performance notes
Motion must fit inside the frame budget (#1 ≤16.6 ms p95); the §6 degradation playbook allows coalescing bubble redraws to every 2nd frame, so the appear transition must tolerate 30 Hz updates.

## Observability
Record whether the announcement opt-in is enabled (as an anonymous settings counter) so we can tell whether the feature is used at all.

title: Spike: bubble instancing cost and LOD ladder at 5 000 visible prints
body:
## Context
US-BIG-003's NFR demands "≥55 fps with 5 000 visible bubbles; instanced rendering", while `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §LOD ladder says the bubble strategy is "Size-threshold raising as density grows; cluster into a single bubble with a count badge — **keep ≤500 visible instances**". Those two statements need reconciling *before* E22-S03 is written: either the engine can genuinely push 5 000 instanced discs inside the frame budget alongside the rest of the R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + stat rows + CVD, roadmap exit criterion #2), or the LOD ladder must engage earlier and the story's AC must be expressed in terms of *qualifying prints* rather than *drawn instances*. Getting this wrong late is expensive — R2's frame budget is a hard exit gate (budgets #1, #2).

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is explicitly **not** expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness may be promoted into the benchmark suite if it proves useful.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness in the chart-engine package rendering N instanced SDF discs (`disc` program, per-instance radius/colour/alpha) over a realistic R2 scene on the reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1), sweeping N ∈ {100, 500, 1 000, 2 500, 5 000, 10 000}.
- Measurements of p50/p95 frame time and fps for each N, both alone and layered on the nominal R2 scene, in Chromium and Electron.
- The point at which the LOD ladder must engage to hold ≥55 fps, and the cost of the count-badge path (SDF text) versus plain discs.
- A recommendation: the visible-instance cap, the size-threshold raising curve, and whether alpha-by-age can be done on the GPU from a per-instance timestamp (avoiding per-frame buffer rewrites).
- An ADR entry recording the decision (feeds E22-T03).

## Out of scope
Production bubble series implementation (E22-S03); tape DOM performance (E22-Q03); heatmap or footprint tuning (E21/E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The question is answered with numbers
  When the sweep completes on reference hardware in both Chromium and Electron
  Then a table of p50/p95 frame time and fps per instance count, alone and layered on the R2 scene, is recorded on the ticket

Scenario: A decision rule is produced
  Given the measured curve
  Then the visible-instance cap and the size-threshold raising curve are stated numerically, and E22-S03's acceptance criteria are rewritten to match before S03 enters Ready

Scenario: The budget cannot be met
  Given fewer than 55 fps even at 500 instances layered on the R2 scene
  Then the spike concludes with an explicit fallback (every-2nd-frame coalescing per 06-performance-and-load-standard.md section 6 item 3, or a reduced default density) and a risk-register update, rather than an optimistic story estimate
```

## Technical notes / design
Per-instance attributes to test: `vec2 posPx`, `float radiusPx`, `vec4 colour`, `float bornAtMs` (for GPU-side alpha decay). Compare two buffer strategies: (a) full rewrite of the instance buffer each frame, (b) ring-buffer append with a per-frame draw range, since bubbles are append-only within a window. Measure the picking cost too — the object index is "a uniform grid (64 px buckets) … radius for bubbles" (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §picking), and a 5 000-object index insertion rate is not free.

## Test plan
Benchmark only; results must be reproducible (three runs, report median) and captured in a form the CI benchmark in E22-Q03 can adopt.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
Measure the cost of the sparse DOM-mirror markers (CMP-195 contract) at the recommended cap — the mirror is affordable precisely because big trades are low-frequency, and this spike must confirm that claim at the cap, not assume it.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 (≤16.6 ms p95) and #2 (never below 30 fps) are the pass/fail lines; report against both.

## Observability
Harness emits the same frame-time histogram shape the engine's production instrumentation uses so numbers are comparable later.

E22-Q01's plan defines *what*; this ticket automates the subset that belongs in E2E — the cross-surface and stateful journeys that unit and component tests cannot cover.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under the web E2E suite, driven by a replayed recorded fixture so runs are deterministic:
  1. **Tape basics** — prints render newest-first with ms timestamps, price, size and side glyph; disconnect shows the disconnected state; resubscribe re-seeds without duplicate rows.
  2. **Pause/resume** — `P` pauses, the buffered count is shown on resume, focus and scroll anchor survive.
  3. **Click-to-locate** — clicking a print moves the crosshair on a synced chart to that timestamp.
  4. **Thresholds** — set notional, percentile and absolute modes; assert the effective absolute threshold is displayed in percentile mode; assert the over-flagging warning appears with a deliberately low threshold.
  5. **Per-symbol memory** — different thresholds on BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT survive symbol switching, reload and a new session.
  6. **Clustering** — turn clustering on, assert merged rows/bubbles with constituent counts, assert the `(estimated)` badge and popover content, change the window and assert immediate recompute.
  7. **Cross-surface agreement** — for one chosen print, assert the tape highlight, the bubble presence and the `GET /market/metrics` value refer to the same print.
  8. **Filters and columns** — filter to sells above a notional, assert chips and the filtered-empty state; enable the cumulative-delta column; reload and assert persistence; run the whole journey keyboard-only.
- Electron-shell run of the critical subset (1, 2, 4, 6) per the strategy's web + Electron requirement.
- Stable selectors (`data-testid`) added where missing, agreed with the story owners.

Perf measurement (E22-Q03); axe/manual a11y audit (E22-Q04) beyond the keyboard-only journey; backend unit/contract tests (E22-T01/T02).

```gherkin

  When the suite runs ten times in CI against the replayed fixture
```

Drive the clock from the replay engine rather than `waitForTimeout`; assert on rendered text and roles rather than CSS. Keep each spec under the suite's per-test time budget; tag the Electron subset so it can be run separately in the nightly job.

## Performance notes
E2E is not a benchmark, but assert the absence of silent loss (the `dropped`/`coalesced_count` indicators appear under burst) so a perf regression surfaces functionally too.

## Context
Two of E22's NFRs are numeric and both feed hard R2 gates: the tape must hold "≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s" (US-BIG-001) and the bubble layer "≥55 fps with 5 000 visible bubbles" (US-BIG-003), while budget #3 — **WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms** — is a hard R2 exit gate measured end-to-end from Bybit WS receipt at the backend to the paint timestamp in the frontend rAF callback (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2). E22-K01 measured the bubble cost in isolation; this ticket turns the measurements into repeatable CI benchmarks and a load profile over the full path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** (CI): bubble series at the instance counts from K01, alone and layered on the R2 reference scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + 3 stat rows + CVD), reporting p50/p95 frame time and fps; fails the build on regression beyond the agreed threshold.
- **Tape benchmark**: replayed burst at 500 / 2 000 / 5 000 prints/s, asserting ≥55 fps, ≤60 DOM rows, bounded worker decode time, and that the ring buffer never loses a print that the frame headers did not report as dropped or coalesced.
- **End-to-end latency harness** for budget #3 on the `trades` path: inject a timestamp at backend WS receipt, correlate with the frontend paint timestamp, report p95/p99 under nominal and realistic-peak load (`06-...` §3.2 definitions).
- **k6/Locust load profile** for the WS fan-out of `trades.{symbol}`: 10 symbols × 5 subscribers at full cadence, asserting backend fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95 (budget #6) and zero message loss (budget #5).
- **Chaos scenarios**: WS disconnect mid-burst; exchange 5xx; Bybit rate-limit `10018`; a 5× synthetic volatility burst for 60 s — assert the UI degrades visibly (coalescing indicator, dropped counters, disconnected state) and never crashes or silently under-reports.
- A results table recorded on the ticket and carried into E22-T03's ADR.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E22-Q02); a11y (E22-Q04); heatmap/footprint benchmarks (E21/E18 own theirs — reuse the harness).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budgets measured, not asserted by feel
  When the benchmarks run on reference hardware
  Then p50 and p95 frame times, fps, and the WS tick to screen p95 and p99 are recorded for every configuration

Scenario: Regression gate
  Given a change that increases bubble draw time beyond the agreed threshold
  When CI runs the engine benchmark
  Then the build fails and names the regressed configuration

Scenario: Degradation is visible under chaos
  Given a 5x synthetic burst for 60 seconds
  Then the app stays above the 30 fps floor or degrades by coalescing, the coalescing factor and dropped counts are displayed, and no print is lost without being counted
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure on the reference machine profile (`06-...` §3.1) and state the hardware in every result; three runs, report the median. Use the replay engine for reproducibility. For budget #3, the Bybit-RTT component is excluded per §3.1 — measure from backend receipt.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test; validate the harness itself by injecting a known 50 ms delay and confirming it appears in the measured p95.

## Security notes
Load tests run against staging only and must respect the exchange rate limits — drive load from recorded fixtures, never by hammering Bybit. A load script pointed at live is a P0 incident; gate it by an environment check in the script itself.

## Accessibility notes
Record whether the announcement opt-in and DOM-mirror markers measurably change frame cost at the cap, so the a11y features are never quietly dropped for performance.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: #1 (≤16.6 ms p95), #2 (never below 30 fps), #3 (WS→screen p95 <100 ms, hard R2 gate), #5 (zero message loss), #6 (≤20 ms fan-out add-on).

## Observability
Publish results as CI artifacts and push the key series into the Grafana perf dashboard so trends are visible across sprints.

Benchmarks merged and running in CI with a regression gate; load profile and chaos scenarios executable on demand and run once for R2; results recorded here and in E22-T03; any budget miss either fixed or recorded as an accepted risk with Owner sign-off in `32-risk-register.md`.

title: Render the time & sales tape panel (SCR-053) at 2 000 prints/s
body:
## Context
Implements **US-BIG-001 — Time & sales tape (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want a raw print feed, so that I can read aggression in real time." This is the host surface of the epic — SCR-053 "Tape / Time & Sales + big-trade bubbles panel" — and every other E22 story hangs off it. The screen contract is already fixed in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`: data from WS `trades.{symbol}`; interactions "click a print → crosshair jumps to that timestamp on synced charts; `Ctrl+F` filter; pause on hover; `P` pause/resume auto-scroll"; states streaming · paused · filtered-empty · disconnected; a11y `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default; performance "virtualised list, ≤60 rows in the DOM, ring buffer of 10 000 prints; bubble layer is part of the chart engine, not DOM".

Design is signed off in E22-D05, which is Done by the end of **Sprint 09**; this story starts in Sprint 12, i.e. the design has been Done for two full sprints (S10, S11), satisfying the design-ahead rule of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 with no Architect/CDO waiver needed.


**Design-ahead:** the consumed design (E22-D05 handoff pack, building on E22-D01..D04) is Status=Done by the end of **Sprint 09**. This story starts in **Sprint 12**, so the design has been Done for two full sprints (Sprint 10 and Sprint 11) — the ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) is met and **no Architect/CDO waiver is claimed**.
## Scope / Deliverables
- Tape organism on SCR-053 built from CMP-049 Table (virtualised), CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; columns time (ms), price, size, notional, taker side with a side glyph, newest first.
- WS subscription to `trades.{symbol}` (binary encoding `cv.v1.msgpack`, kind 3) via the shared worker described in `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §"The WS client runs in a shared worker so that multiple chart instances (and the DOM ladder) decode each frame once".
- Ring buffer of 10 000 prints in the worker, with ≤60 rows rendered in the DOM; per-frame coalescing of incoming batches and a visible **coalescing-factor indicator** driven by `coalesced_count` (§"A coalesced frame sets `coalesced: true` … the UI uses this to drive the 'feed compressed' indicator … rather than silently under-reporting activity").
- Pause model per the D05 spec: hover-pause and explicit `P`; while paused the tape freezes for inspection **while continuing to buffer**, and on resume shows how many prints were buffered (US-BIG-001 scenario 3).
- States: streaming; paused ("Paused — 412 prints buffered"); disconnected/stale; **partial history** naming the first available recorded timestamp (global AC #7).
- Click-to-locate: clicking (or `Enter` on) a row moves the crosshair on synced charts to that timestamp.
- Analytics: `tape.paused`, `tape.resumed`, `tape.print_clicked`.
- Storybook stories for the tape organism covering each state, and the accessible table alternative reachable from the panel header.

## Out of scope
Threshold highlighting (E22-S02), bubbles (E22-S03), clustering controls (E22-S04), filters/column picker (E22-S05), alerts (E22-S06), click-to-trade (E31), speed-of-tape gauge (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tape renders
  Given a subscription to trades.BTCUSDT
  Then each print shows time with millisecond precision, price, size and taker side with a side glyph, newest first
  And the side is taken from the feed's aggressor side, never inferred client-side

Scenario: High rate
  Given 2000 prints per second
  Then the tape coalesces per frame without dropping rows from the underlying ring buffer
  And the coalescing factor is displayed
  And the panel sustains at least 55 fps with no more than 60 rows in the DOM

Scenario: Pause and inspect
  When I pause the tape
  Then it freezes for inspection while continuing to buffer
  And resuming shows how many prints were buffered

Scenario: Disconnected
  Given the WebSocket drops
  Then the tape shows a disconnected state with the time of the last received print, and on resubscribe the snapshot of the last 200 prints reseeds the view without duplicating rows

Scenario: Partial history
  Given the recorder has data only from a timestamp later than the requested window start
  Then the panel shows an explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
Decode once in the shared worker and transfer typed arrays to the panel; never JSON-parse per print on the main thread. Render with a windowed virtualiser keyed on a stable print id so React does not re-key the whole list per frame. Deduplicate by `tradeId` on snapshot re-delivery after a reconnect. Timestamps render in the user's configured timezone with millisecond precision; use `font.mono` for numeric columns (CMP-049 token contract). The panel must not implement any threshold logic — the big-trade flag arrives from the server (E22-T02).

## Test plan
- Unit: ring-buffer eviction at 10 000; dedupe on snapshot overlap; pause buffering count; coalescing-factor computation from `coalesced_count`; timestamp/locale formatting.
- Component (Storybook + testing-library): each state renders its documented copy string; row click emits `tape.print_clicked` and the crosshair sync call.
- E2E (Playwright, added in E22-Q02): pause/resume via `P`, click-to-locate, reconnect.
- Perf (E22-Q03): 2 000 prints/s replay fixture, assert ≥55 fps and ≤60 DOM rows.
- a11y: axe-core on the panel; manual screen-reader pass.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Market data is **public**; the subscription still requires an authenticated session and `marketdata:read` (global AC #1). Do not render exchange error codes raw — surface an actionable message with the code behind a details disclosure (global AC #5). No user input is echoed into the DOM except the symbol, which is validated against the instruments cache.

## Accessibility notes
`role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default; opt-in polite announcements for whale prints only, throttled per the E22-D04 spec. Rows individually focusable with `↑/↓` navigation and visible focus; focus is preserved across pause/resume. All columns readable as a table by a screen reader; the accessible table alternative is reachable from the panel header. Side is conveyed by glyph **and** colour. Targets ≥24×24 px. `prefers-reduced-motion` disables row-insert animation entirely.

## Performance notes
≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s (US-BIG-001 NFR); ≤60 DOM rows and a 10 000-print ring buffer (SCR-053); contributes to the hard R2 gate WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms (budget #3) — instrument the paint timestamp so Q03 can measure it.

## Observability
Client metrics: rendered-rows-per-frame, decode time per frame, dropped/coalesced counts surfaced from the frame headers. Analytics events `tape.paused`, `tape.resumed`, `tape.print_clicked`.

## Definition of Done
All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests or an executed QA step; coverage ≥80 %; axe green + manual SR spot-check; design-QA comparison against the E22-D05 pack (formally swept in E22-D06); perf benchmark recorded; QA sign-off comment; demoed at Sprint Review on staging (demo); feature flag `orderflow.tape` recorded with its per-environment default; PRs merged via merge queue.

body:
## Context
Implements **US-BIG-002 — Big-trade threshold highlighting (Must)**: large prints must stand out by size, with the threshold expressible as an absolute size, a USDT notional, or a percentile of the recent distribution. The NFR is the load-bearing part: "thresholds per symbol; **evaluation backend-side so tape, bubbles and alerts agree**". This story is therefore a *control surface plus persistence*, not a calculation: it sets the subscription options and renders the flag the server already computed in E22-T01/T02.

The roadmap's E22 line names "per-symbol threshold memory" explicitly as scope.


**Design-ahead:** the consumed design (E22-D05 handoff pack, building on E22-D01..D04) is Status=Done by the end of **Sprint 09**. This story starts in **Sprint 12**, so the design has been Done for two full sprints (Sprint 10 and Sprint 11) — the ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) is met and **no Architect/CDO waiver is claimed**.
## Scope / Deliverables
- Threshold control strip on SCR-053 (`min` / `whale` inputs and the mode selector), built from the design-system inputs specified in E22-D05.
- Three modes wired to the subscription options: `absolute_size`, `notional`, `percentile` (with a window selector, default 1 h).
- Display of the **effective absolute threshold** whenever percentile mode is active, updating as the distribution moves (US-BIG-002 scenario 2).
- Size-tier highlighting in the tape: marker + size label, tiers encoded by weight/glyph as well as colour.
- Over-flagging warning: when the server reports `threshold_too_low` (>20 % of prints flagged), show the warning with the suggested value and cap highlighting to preserve legibility (US-BIG-002 scenario 3).
- Per-symbol persistence in Postgres `settings` (`scope='user'`) under keys `bigtrade.threshold_mode`, `bigtrade.threshold_value`, `bigtrade.percentile_window_ms`, with per-symbol values held in the JSONB `value` object; restoring a symbol restores its own threshold.
- Analytics + audit: `settings.change` audit entry on persistence (global AC #2).

## Out of scope
Threshold evaluation itself (E22-T01); clustering controls (E22-S04); bubbles (E22-S03); alert thresholds (E22-S06/E40); a global cross-symbol default preset library.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Manual threshold
  Given the threshold is 250000 USDT notional
  Then qualifying prints are highlighted with a marker and a size label in the tape
  And the highlight is driven by the server-provided flag, with no client-side comparison of notional against the threshold

Scenario: Percentile threshold
  When I choose the 99th percentile over a 1 hour window
  Then the effective absolute threshold is displayed and updates as the distribution moves

Scenario: Threshold too low
  Given the threshold would flag more than 20 percent of prints
  Then a warning suggests raising it and highlighting is capped to preserve legibility

Scenario: Per-symbol memory
  Given BTCUSDT is set to 250000 notional and ETHUSDT to 100000 notional
  When I switch symbols back and forth
  Then each symbol restores its own threshold without re-entry, surviving a page reload and a new session

Scenario: Invalid input
  When I enter a negative or non-numeric threshold
  Then the control shows an inline validation message, the previous value is retained, and no subscription change is sent
```

## Technical notes / design
Changing the mode or value re-subscribes (or sends a subscription update) to `trades.{symbol}` with new options and re-seeds from the snapshot — do **not** re-filter the local buffer against a locally computed threshold, because percentile mode has no client-side definition and the three surfaces would drift. Settings keys must satisfy the Postgres constraint `st_key_fmt` `^[a-z0-9_]+([.][a-z0-9_]+){0,4}$` and are written with `value_type='object'`; debounce writes (500 ms) so dragging a stepper does not produce an audit storm. Percentile windows depend on recorded history — when the recorder has less history than the window, show the partial-history state (global AC #7) rather than a silently short window.


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 2 → 1 pt: the form is assembled entirely from existing design-system controls (CMP-016/CMP-021/CMP-011) against the settings keys already fixed by E22-D05, and all evaluation logic lives in E22-T01 — this story is wiring plus persistence. Total S/T/K engineering points for E22 are held at 22, inside the ±15% band around the roadmap's 21 pts for this epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 122/313).

## Test plan
- Unit: mode↔option mapping; validation table (negative, zero, non-numeric, percentile >100); debounce; per-symbol settings read/write and merge semantics.
- Component: effective-threshold display updates on config echo; over-flagging warning appears and caps highlighting.
- Integration: settings round-trip through the API with an audit entry written.
- E2E (E22-Q02): set per-symbol thresholds, switch symbols, reload, assert restoration.
- Coverage ≥80 %.

## Security notes
Threshold values are user settings — validate server-side as well as client-side (never trust the client bound), enforce RBAC on the settings endpoint, and confirm `settings.change` audit entries carry actor, timestamp and redacted payload (global AC #2). Bounds exist to prevent the DoS path identified in E22-X01 (a zero/negative threshold subscribing to everything on a hot symbol).

## Accessibility notes
Numeric inputs are properly labelled with units in the accessible name ("Minimum notional, USDT"); validation messages are associated via `aria-describedby` and announced; the over-flagging warning is a status message (WCAG 4.1.3) announced once, not a colour change; size tiers never rely on colour alone; controls reachable and operable by keyboard with ≥24×24 px targets.

## Performance notes
A threshold change must re-seed within one snapshot round-trip and must not stall the tape; percentile updates arrive at most every 5 s from the server and must not trigger a full list re-render.

## Observability
`bigtrade_threshold_changed_total{mode}` (client analytics), server-side `bigtrade_threshold_advisory_total`; audit `settings.change`.

Scenarios automated; coverage met; settings keys documented in `21-database-schema.md` §3.9 usage notes; axe green; design-QA comparison; QA sign-off; demoed; flag `orderflow.tape` shared with S01; PR merged.

title: Draw big-trade bubbles on the chart (CMP-112) with linear/log scaling
body:
## Context
Implements **US-BIG-003 — Bubble plotting on the chart (Must)**: "I want big trades drawn as bubbles on the chart, so that size is visible in price context." This is the epic's chart-engine deliverable and the reason `26-chart-engine-design.md` lists "Bubbles | instanced circles (SDF disc) | `disc` | 1 | Radius by notional, alpha by age" in its draw-call table and "big-trade bubbles" among the surfaces that justified the custom engine at all (ADR-0002). The LOD ladder ("Size-threshold raising as density grows; cluster into a single bubble with a count badge | Keep ≤500 visible instances") and the measurements from E22-K01 define how density is handled.


**Design-ahead:** the consumed design (E22-D05 handoff pack, building on E22-D01..D04) is Status=Done by the end of **Sprint 09**. This story starts in **Sprint 12**, so the design has been Done for two full sprints (Sprint 10 and Sprint 11) — the ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) is met and **no Architect/CDO waiver is claimed**.
## Scope / Deliverables
- A bubble **series plugin** in the chart-engine package (`kind: 'bubbles'`, per the engine's `SeriesOptions` union which already includes `'bubbles'` and a `BubbleOptions` entry), consuming the same server-flagged prints the tape uses — one data path, not a second subscription with its own thresholds.
- CMP-112 BigTradeBubble implementation matching the E22-D03/D05 spec: shapes `circle|square|diamond|text`, `sizeScale: "linear"|"log"` with the specified radius curves and clamps, side encoded by **shape and colour**, alpha-by-age.
- Instanced rendering through the `disc` program with per-instance position, radius, colour and birth timestamp; the buffer strategy chosen by E22-K01.
- LOD ladder: raise the size threshold as density grows and collapse to a single bubble with a count badge at the cap measured in K01.
- Legend stating the active scale and the size-to-notional mapping (US-BIG-003 scenario 2).
- Picking: bubbles registered in the engine's uniform-grid object index (radius test) so hover/click yields a detail tooltip with time, price, size, notional, side and — when clustered — the constituent count.
- Sparse DOM-mirror markers per the CMP-195 contract with `aria-label` "Big {side}, {notional} USDT, {price}, {time}".
- Storybook stories: Circle, Square, Diamond, TextMode, LogScale.

## Out of scope
Clustering computation (E22-T01) and its controls (E22-S04); the tape itself (S01); liquidation markers (E24); detector markers (E25); any trading action from a bubble (E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bubbles drawn
  Then each qualifying print draws at its price and time, with radius scaled by notional and side encoded by shape and colour
  And the radius curve matches the specification in the signed-off design pack

Scenario: Scale control
  When I switch to log scaling
  Then extreme prints stop dominating the view and the legend states that the log scale is active

Scenario: Dense cluster
  Given many qualifying prints coincide
  Then clustering per US-BIG-004 applies and a single bubble with a count badge is drawn rather than overlapping bubbles

Scenario: Density ceiling
  Given the number of qualifying prints in view exceeds the measured visible-instance cap
  Then the LOD ladder raises the size threshold and collapses the remainder, the chart holds at least 55 fps, and the legend indicates that smaller prints are hidden at this zoom

Scenario: Hover and keyboard inspection
  When I hover a bubble or focus its DOM-mirror marker
  Then a detail tooltip shows time, price, size, notional, side and constituent count, and the same information is available to a screen reader
```

## Technical notes / design
Radius: `linear` → `r = clamp(r_min + k*notional, r_min, r_max)`; `log` → `r = clamp(r_min + k*ln(1 + notional/n0), r_min, r_max)` — constants come from the design pack, not from taste. Alpha-by-age is computed in the shader from a per-instance `bornAtMs` and a uniform `nowMs`, so ageing costs no buffer rewrites. Bubbles are append-only within the visible window; use the ring-buffer/draw-range strategy validated in K01. Time positioning uses the print's own timestamp, not its bar's — a bubble sits where the print happened; a *cluster's* bubble sits at its first print (consistent with the bar-attribution rule in US-BIG-004). Coalescing bubble redraws to every 2nd frame is permitted under `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §6 item 3 when the frame budget is under pressure.


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 3 → 2 pts: the instanced-disc draw path, the LOD ladder and the DOM-mirror marker contract are all delivered by E11/E22-K01; this story consumes them for one new mark type rather than building new engine machinery. Total S/T/K engineering points for E22 are held at 22, inside the ±15% band around the roadmap's 21 pts for this epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 122/313).

## Test plan
- Unit: radius curves (both scales, at bounds and beyond clamps); LOD threshold raising; count-badge aggregation; picking hit-test at edges and overlapping radii.
- Visual: golden images per shape and per scale, and at the LOD cap.
- Perf: 5 000 qualifying prints in view — assert ≥55 fps and that the visible-instance cap holds; layered on the full R2 scene assert ≥30 fps floor (budget #2).
- a11y: axe on the DOM-mirror output; keyboard traversal of markers.
- Coverage ≥85 % on the engine package.

## Security notes
Public market data. The bubble layer must never accept a threshold from the client-side layer — it renders server-flagged prints only, which is also what prevents a malicious/buggy client from making the server stream unfiltered prints. No user-controlled string reaches the shader or the glyph atlas without length bounds (tooltip text is DOM, escaped by React).

## Accessibility notes
Sparse DOM-mirror markers are affordable here because big trades are low-frequency (CMP-112 catalogue note) — confirm the marker count stays within the K01-measured budget at the cap. Side must be distinguishable by shape in greyscale; the legend text is real text, not an image; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the appear transition and the alpha decay animation (values snap).

**Design-ahead:** the consumed design (E22-D05 handoff pack, building on E22-D01..D04) is Status=Done by the end of **Sprint 09**. The clustering algorithm and its determinism guarantees (E22-T01, E22-T04); iceberg/split-fill detection (E25 — deliberately distinct from display clustering, as `/market/trades` notes).

```gherkin
Scenario: Clustered
  Given the window is 250 ms and the price tolerance is 1 tick

  When I set the window to 1 second

Scenario: Cluster crossing a bar boundary
  Then the cluster is attributed to the bar containing its first print, and this rule is stated in the tooltip

  Given clustering is active
  Then the (estimated) badge is visible with the literal word "estimated" in its accessible name

  Given the window is set to 0
```

Never re-cluster locally: the constituent count and the merged size arrive as `cluster_size` (JSON) / `flags` bit2 (binary kind 3) from the server, which is what keeps the tape, the bubbles and any future alert in agreement. Bounds are enforced server-side too (E22-T02); the client must not send out-of-range values and must surface the server's rejection as an actionable message (global AC #5). Public data, no secrets.

The `(estimated)` badge is focusable, opens its popover with `Enter`, and its accessible name contains the literal word "estimated" — it may never be conveyed by colour, icon or opacity alone (CMP-227 contract). A window change costs one re-subscribe plus a 200-print snapshot; it must not drop the tape below the ≥55 fps floor or clear the ring buffer.

`bigtrade_cluster_config_changed_total` (analytics); server-side `bigtrade_clusters_emitted_total`; audit `settings.change`.

Implements **US-BIG-006 — Tape filters and columns (Should)**: "I want to filter and configure the tape, so that it shows only what I care about." ## Scope / Deliverables
- FilterBar (CMP-055) with removable chips (CMP-011): filter by side, by minimum size/notional, and by aggregated-vs-raw prints; `Ctrl+F` focuses the filter input (SCR-053 interaction contract).
- ColumnPicker (CMP-056): show/hide/reorder columns; column set includes time, price, size, notional, side, and a **cumulative-delta column** (US-BIG-006 scenario 2); reorder by drag **and** `Alt+↑/↓`.

- Filtered-empty state with the documented copy ("No prints above 10 000 USDT in the last 5 min") and a clear-filter action.
- Buffer-size control with a live **memory estimate** (e.g. "10 000 prints ≈ 2.4 MB").
- Analytics: `tape.filter_changed` (size/side/aggregation).

## Out of scope
Server-side `min_size` thresholds (E22-S02 — a display filter never changes the subscription); export of the tape (not in scope for E22; the Deep-Stats CSV export is E20); cumulative-delta computation itself (E23 supplies `cvd`/per-bar delta — this story only renders the value it receives).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Filter by size and side
  When I filter to sells above 50000 USDT
  Then only matching prints display and the active filter is shown as a removable chip
  And the underlying buffered store is unchanged, so clearing the filter restores the hidden prints immediately

Scenario: Column set

Scenario: Filter yields nothing

Scenario: Buffer size and memory
  When I change the buffer size
  Then an estimated memory figure is shown alongside it and the ring buffer is resized without dropping the currently visible rows

Scenario: Keyboard-only operation
  When I use only the keyboard
  Then I can focus the filter with Ctrl+F, add and remove filter chips, and reorder columns with Alt+Up/Alt+Down
```

## Technical notes / design
Filtering runs over the worker-side ring buffer and returns an index list to the virtualiser — do not copy the buffer per keystroke; debounce the filter input (150 ms). Column reorder writes to the pane's layout config; keep the column ids stable so saved layouts survive future column additions (unknown ids are ignored with a log, not an error). Memory estimate is computed from the fixed per-print record size, not measured — state that it is an estimate in the label.


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 2 → 1 pt: filtering is an index-list predicate over the ring buffer that E22-S01 already owns, and the column picker is stock CMP-056 — no new data path. ## Test plan
- Unit: filter predicate composition (side + size + aggregated); index-list virtualiser integration; buffer resize preserving visible rows; memory-estimate arithmetic.
- Component: chip add/remove; filtered-empty copy; column reorder by keyboard and by drag; persistence round-trip.
- E2E (E22-Q02): filter, reload, assert restoration; keyboard-only path.
- a11y: axe; `role="group"` `aria-label="Active filters"` on the FilterBar (CMP-055 contract); checkbox-list semantics in the ColumnPicker.
- Coverage ≥80 %.

## Security notes
Filter values are local and never reach the server, so there is no injection surface; still validate numeric input and cap the buffer size (an unbounded buffer is a client memory-exhaustion path, related to the DoS branch of E22-X01). Layout persistence goes through the existing authenticated, RBAC-checked layout API and writes an audit entry per global AC #2.

FilterBar is `role="group"` labelled "Active filters" with keyboard-removable chips; ColumnPicker uses the CMP-041 Menu checkbox-list pattern with `Alt+↑/↓` reordering; the filtered-empty state is announced as a status message; all controls ≥24×24 px with visible focus.

## Performance notes
Filtering must not drop the tape below ≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s; the predicate runs in the worker, not on the main thread. Buffer resize is O(n) once, not per frame.

## Observability
`tape.filter_changed` analytics with the filter shape (not the raw values); client counter for filter evaluation time per frame.

Scenarios automated; coverage met; axe green + keyboard-only pass; design-QA comparison; QA sign-off; demoed; layout persistence documented; PR merged.

title: Big-trade (whale) alerts with flood control
body:
## Context
Implements **US-BIG-005 — Big-trade alerts (Should)**: "I want an alert on very large prints, so that I do not have to watch the tape constantly." Its `Deps` are `US-BIG-002, US-ALRT-004`, and US-ALRT-004 (Alert centre) ships with **E40 Alerts** in R3 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7). This story is therefore deliberately parked in `Backlog` with milestone R3: E22 ships the *metric* (`big_trade_notional`, registered by E22-T01) that the alert condition consumes, and the alert itself is delivered once the alert centre, delivery channels and snooze/mute machinery exist. Shipping a bespoke alert path inside E22 would create the second implementation this epic exists to avoid.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A big-trade alert condition available in the alert editor (SCR-091) using the `big_trade_notional` metric with a **second, higher threshold** independent of the tape's highlight threshold (the story's example: 1 000 000 USDT).
- Alert payload: symbol, side, price, size and time of the triggering print.
- Sound and per-symbol mute: a muted symbol still records the alert in the alert centre but plays no sound.
- Flood control: when more than 10 qualifying prints occur within 10 seconds, aggregate into a single summary alert carrying the count; the aggregation window and count are configurable.
- Components per the traceability matrix for SCR-091: CMP-008, CMP-009, CMP-040, CMP-065, CMP-157, CMP-164, CMP-219, CMP-234.

## Out of scope
The alert centre, delivery channels, snooze/quiet hours (E40 / US-ALRT-004..006); the tape and bubble surfaces (E22-S01..S05); rule-engine actions (E35–E37).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Whale alert
  Given a second threshold of 1000000 USDT
  Then crossing prints raise an alert with symbol, side, price, size and time

Scenario: Sound and mute
  When I enable sound and later mute the symbol
  Then the alert still appears in the alert centre but plays no sound

Scenario: Flood control
  Given more than 10 qualifying prints occur in 10 seconds
  Then alerts are aggregated into a single summary alert with a count

Scenario: Threshold independence
  Given the tape highlight threshold is 250000 and the alert threshold is 1000000
  Then a 400000 print highlights in the tape and on the chart but raises no alert
```

## Technical notes / design
Evaluate against the same `BigTradeEngine` output as the tape and the bubbles — the alert threshold is a second comparison on the same metric, not a second engine. Flood control is a token-bucket per (symbol, alert) emitting a summary event when the bucket is exhausted; the summary must state the suppressed count so nothing is silently dropped.


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 3 → 2 pts: the alert centre, delivery, mute and persistence all belong to E40; this story adds one condition over the existing `big_trade_notional` metric plus a token-bucket flood control. Total S/T/K engineering points for E22 are held at 22, inside the ±15% band around the roadmap's 21 pts for this epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 122/313).

## Test plan
Unit: threshold independence; flood-control aggregation boundaries (exactly 10 in 10 s, 11 in 10 s, 10 in 11 s); mute semantics. Integration with the alert centre's persistence and delivery. E2E: create the alert, fire it against a replayed fixture, assert the alert centre record and the absence of sound when muted. Latency test per the NFR.

## Security notes
Alerts are per-user and RBAC-scoped by the alert centre; alert creation writes `alerts.create` to the audit log (`21-database-schema.md` audit action list). No market-data secret exposure. Flood control also serves as an abuse/DoS control on notification channels.

## Accessibility notes

title: Implement BigTradeEngine: thresholds, percentiles and deterministic clustering
body:
## Context
US-BIG-002 NFR: "thresholds per symbol; **evaluation backend-side so tape, bubbles and alerts agree**". US-BIG-004 NFR: "deterministic and unit-tested; **clustering happens once, backend-side**". This task builds the single engine that both statements demand, inside module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` — "orderflow/ # footprint, profile, cvd, imbalance, heatmap, tape"). Everything else in E22 — the tape highlight, the chart bubbles, the future alert condition — renders this engine's output.

Input is the normalised trade stream produced by E08 (US-MKT-006: each print normalised to `{ts, price, qty, side, tradeId}`, published on the internal bus exactly once, idempotent by `tradeId`). Bybit supplies the aggressor side directly (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`: "Bybit gives the **aggressor side directly** (`S`), so no tick-rule reconstruction is needed — this is the single most important simplification in the whole order-flow stack"), so side is **exact**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/bigtrade.py`: `BigTradeEngine` with per-symbol config and three threshold modes — `absolute_size` (base units), `notional` (price × size, USDT), `percentile` (rank over a rolling window, default 3 600 000 ms).
- Rolling percentile estimator: a bounded-memory streaming quantile (t-digest or P²) over print notionals, publishing the **effective absolute threshold** so the UI can display it (US-BIG-002 scenario 2) and refreshing at most every 5 s.
- Over-flagging guard: when the flagged fraction over the trailing window exceeds **20 %**, emit a `threshold_too_low` advisory with a suggested value and cap highlighting (US-BIG-002 scenario 3).
- Deterministic cluster state machine: per `(symbol, side, price_bucket)` open cluster with a `window_ms` deadline and `tolerance_ticks` bucket width (tick size from the instruments-info cache); merge on same side + within tolerance of the anchor price + inside the deadline; else emit and open a new cluster. **Bar attribution: the cluster belongs to the bar containing its first print** (US-BIG-004 scenario 3).
- Immediate recompute on config change: changing the window recomputes clustering from the stored prints without a restart (US-BIG-004 scenario 2).
- Metric descriptors registered in `MetricRegistry` per `24-internal-schemas.md`: `big_trade_notional` (largest print notional in window, `window_ms=1000`, exact), `big_trade_zscore` (z-score of print size vs rolling mean, `window=500 trades`, `z_threshold=3.0`, exact), `trade_cluster` (`window_ms=50` default, confidence **estimated**).
- Outputs on the internal bus consumed by E22-T02 (wire) and by E40's alert evaluator later.

## Out of scope
Wire encoding and endpoints (E22-T02); UI (S01–S05); speed-of-tape and iceberg detection (E25); liquidation prints (E24).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Notional threshold flags exactly the right prints
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT window and a threshold of 250000 USDT notional
  When the window is processed
  Then the set of flagged print ids equals the set computed by an independent DuckDB query over the Parquet tier with WHERE notional >= 250000

Scenario: Percentile mode publishes its effective threshold
  Given percentile mode at the 99th percentile over a 1 hour window
  Then each emitted config echo carries the current effective absolute threshold
  And the estimator's value is within 1 percent of an exact quantile over the same window

Scenario: Clustering is deterministic
  Given cluster_window_ms = 250 and cluster_tolerance_ticks = 1
  When the same recorded window is processed twice, including once with prints delivered in differently-sized batches
  Then the emitted clusters are identical in count, membership, aggregate size and attributed bar

Scenario: A cluster spanning a bar boundary
  Given a cluster whose first print is in bar N and whose last print is in bar N+1
  Then the cluster is attributed to bar N

Scenario: Over-flagging is caught
  Given a threshold that flags more than 20 percent of prints over the trailing window
  Then a threshold_too_low advisory with a suggested value is emitted and highlighting is capped

Scenario: Duplicate print after reconnect
  Given the same tradeId is delivered twice after a resubscribe
  Then it is counted once in thresholds, clustering and metrics
```

## Technical notes / design
Config shape (mirrors the WS options in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 so there is one vocabulary):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BigTradeConfig:
    mode: Literal["absolute_size", "notional", "percentile"] = "notional"
    value: Decimal = Decimal("250000")       # units depend on mode; percentile => 0..100
    percentile_window_ms: int = 3_600_000
    cluster_window_ms: int = 0               # 0 disables clustering
    cluster_tolerance_ticks: int = 0
```
Determinism rules: process prints in `(ts, tradeId)` order; never use wall-clock time in the state machine — deadlines are evaluated against print timestamps so replay and live take the same path (R2 exit criterion #1: one shared pipeline for live and replay). Use `Decimal` for price/size arithmetic, consistent with the `Decimal` string types in the API and WS schemas. Price bucketing: `bucket = floor(price / (tick_size * max(1, tolerance_ticks)))` with the anchor price retained for display. Memory: bounded ring per symbol sized by `max(percentile_window_ms, cluster_window_ms)` and a hard cap; emit a metric when the cap truncates.

## Test plan
- Unit: each threshold mode; percentile estimator accuracy vs exact quantile on synthetic and recorded distributions; cluster merge/emit boundaries (exactly at the deadline, one tick outside tolerance, opposite side); bar attribution across boundaries; duplicate `tradeId`; config change mid-stream; empty and single-print windows; `cluster_window_ms=0` short-circuit.
- Property: batching invariance (same prints, different batch splits → identical output); ordering invariance under `(ts, tradeId)` sort.
- Integration: recorded fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- Coverage target ≥85 % on `server/orderflow/bigtrade.py`.

## Security notes
Bounds-check every config value at the engine boundary (`cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, percentile 0–100, non-negative threshold) so a malformed subscription cannot allocate unbounded state — this is the primary DoS control identified in the epic's STRIDE (E22-X01). Market data is classification **public**; no secrets touched.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend).

## Performance notes
Evaluation must add ≤2 ms p95 to the ingest→bus path (US-MKT-006 NFR: ingest→bus ≤20 ms p95 total) and sustain 5 000 prints/s across subscribed symbols without loss (budget #5). Per-symbol memory must stay inside budget #8 (≤300 MB per actively-recorded symbol, shared with book state and bar builders).

## Observability
`bigtrade_prints_evaluated_total{symbol}`, `bigtrade_flagged_total{symbol,mode}`, `bigtrade_clusters_emitted_total{symbol}`, `bigtrade_eval_latency_seconds`, `bigtrade_state_truncated_total{symbol}`, `bigtrade_threshold_advisory_total{symbol}`. Span `orderflow.bigtrade.evaluate` nested in the ingest span.

## Definition of Done
AC verified by the tests above; coverage ≥85 %; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` metric table updated if any descriptor default changed; docstrings for the clustering rules; no demo needed beyond the parity evidence from E22-T04; PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

`E08` normalised trade stream + instruments-info tick size; `E22-X01` STRIDE bounds must be known before the config validation is written.

## Context
The contracts this epic needs are already specified and must be *implemented*, not redesigned. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 defines `trades.{symbol}` with options `min_size`, `cluster_window_ms`, `cluster_tolerance_ticks`, snapshot "Last 200 prints", default throttle 100 ms, binary `body_kind 3`; §14.2 defines `TradesBatch` with `cluster_size`, `is_block_trade`, `is_liquidation`, `tick_direction` and `dropped` ("Prints filtered out by `min_size` since the previous frame; **never silent**"); §3.4 fixes the 22-byte binary record with `flags` bit0 block trade, bit1 liquidation-origin, **bit2 cluster-aggregated**. REST side: `GET /market/trades` (`side`, `min_size`, `cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, cursor pagination) and `GET /market/metrics` for `big_trade_notional` / `big_trade_zscore`. Interface-first rule (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) applies: any diff to these documents is drafted and reviewed before implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Subscribe/ack path: echo the effective options in the `ok` response (`effective: { throttle_ms, encoding, min_size, cluster_window_ms, cluster_tolerance_ticks }`) and reject out-of-range options with a topic-scoped error rather than clamping silently.
- Extend the big-trade flag and the effective absolute threshold into the subscription echo so tape and bubbles never recompute a threshold client-side.
- REST: implement `GET /market/trades` filters and clustering (delegating to the same engine), and register `big_trade_notional` / `big_trade_zscore` in `GET /market/metrics`.
- Contract tests against the OpenAPI document and the WS JSON Schemas; update `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` if a field is genuinely missing (e.g. the effective-threshold echo) via a reviewed diff.

## Out of scope
Engine logic (E22-T01); any UI; alert delivery (E40); liquidation topic (E24).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given a subscription to trades.BTCUSDT with min_size 0.5
  When prints below 0.5 arrive
  Then they are excluded from the frame and the frame's dropped counter reports exactly how many were excluded since the previous frame

Scenario: Clustering is signalled on both encodings
  Given cluster_window_ms 250 and cluster_tolerance_ticks 1
  Then JSON frames carry cluster_size greater than 1 for merged prints and binary kind 3 records set flags bit2
  And a client decoding either encoding reconstructs identical cluster membership counts

Scenario: Out-of-range options are rejected
  Given a subscription with cluster_window_ms 999999
  Then the subscribe response is ok false with a topic-scoped error naming the parameter and its allowed range, and no subscription is created

Scenario: REST and WS agree
  Given the same window requested over GET /market/trades and captured live over trades.BTCUSDT with identical options
  Then the flagged print set and the cluster membership are identical

Scenario: Coalescing is visible
  Given a burst that forces frames to coalesce
  Then coalesced is true and coalesced_count reports the number of merged source updates, and no print is lost from the batch
```

## Technical notes / design
Keep the 100 ms default throttle for `trades.{symbol}`; the snapshot is the last 200 prints. Binary record layout (do not deviate): `u32 ts_offset_ms`, `i64 price` (scaled), `u64 size` (scaled), `u8 side` (0 buy, 1 sell), `u8 flags`. Client obligations from §3.4 are mirrored in the contract tests: a body whose length disagrees with `record_count` is `frame_malformed`. `permessage-deflate` stays **off** for `cv.v1.msgpack` and on for JSON. RBAC: both endpoints carry `x-rbac: { permissions: [marketdata:read], scope: none }` — enforce server-side per global AC #1 (403 + audit, no state change).


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 3 → 2 pts: the WS envelope, framing, sequencing and REST pagination conventions are already established by E17; this task adds options and one payload to an existing topic. Total S/T/K engineering points for E22 are held at 22, inside the ±15% band around the roadmap's 21 pts for this epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 122/313).

## Test plan
- Contract: OpenAPI schema validation for `/market/trades` and `/market/metrics`; JSON-Schema validation of every emitted `TradesBatch`; binary round-trip decode of kind 3 including flags.
- Unit: `dropped` accounting across frame boundaries; option validation table (min/max/типы); effective-option echo.
- Integration: recorded fixtures incl. disconnect+resync (snapshot re-delivery) and sequence gap.
- Load: 2 000 prints/s on one symbol with 5 subscribers; assert zero lost prints and bounded frame sizes (§3.6 frame size limits).
- Coverage ≥85 % on the touched API/WS modules.

This is the epic's main DoS surface (STRIDE-D, E22-X01): enforce the documented parameter bounds, the per-connection subscription cap, and `Limit`/cursor pagination on the REST path; a `min_size=0` subscription on a hot symbol must be shed by throttling and coalescing rather than by unbounded buffering. Reject unknown options instead of ignoring them. Data classification public; RBAC still required.
